turn_text: If you're a doctor and you're awakened to what's happened, if you know that it's wrong and it's not right, Don't sit by the sidelines anymore. Don't let just Peter McCulloch and Dr. Malone and Pierre Corrie and all these courageous doctors who have stepped forward to warn the public, they need help. We literally need thousands of doctors who are aware of the problem. To join together, there are safety and numbers and be honest and truthful with the American public. I'm begging doctors, I'm begging nurses to come forward, join together as one massive group and put an end to this insanity and help restore yourselves to the position that I think you all thought you'd be in going through medical school and taking that Hippocratic oath. being loyal first to your patients and being the one to call the shots when it comes to how you care for your patients. I'm begging doctors, you have to step up the plate.

explicit_propositions.text: If you are a doctor and you are awakened to what has happened, then you should act.
The current situation is morally wrong and unjustifiable.
Doctors who recognize the wrongdoing should not remain passive observers.
Peter McCulloch, Dr. Malone, and Pierre Corrie are courageous doctors who have spoken out.
There is a critical need for thousands of additional doctors to become involved.
Collective action among doctors will enhance safety and effectiveness.
Honesty and truthfulness toward the American public are necessary.
Medical professionals should prioritize patient loyalty over institutional allegiance.
The Hippocratic Oath obligates physicians to act ethically on behalf of their patients.
Doctors and nurses are currently failing in their ethical duty to speak out.

assumptions.text: Doctors possess sufficient moral agency to recognize and respond to ethical violations.
Public trust in medicine depends on transparency and collective professional integrity.
A large-scale coordinated effort by healthcare providers can effectively challenge systemic failures.
The speaker believes that many doctors are currently complicit due to silence rather than ignorance.
The audience (doctors and nurses) values the ideals of medical professionalism and the Hippocratic Oath.
Moral appeals are effective motivators for professional action in high-stakes ethical contexts.
Truth-telling to the public is a legitimate and necessary form of professional responsibility.
Institutional pressures do not fully override individual physician autonomy in ethical decision-making.
The speaker sees themselves as having moral authority to appeal to other medical professionals.
The term 'insanity' refers to a widespread, rational failure within the medical system that demands intervention.
